facts.text: The only player of the 1960s to rush for 1,500 yards was Jim Brown — and he did it twice (1963: 1,863 yds; 1965: 1,544 yds).
The only player of the 1960s to carry the ball 300 times: Jim Brown, 1961 — 305 carries.
The only player of the 1960s to gain 2,000 yards from scrimmage: Jim Brown, 1963 — 2,131 scrimmage yds.
The only player of the 1960s to rush for 1,000 yards at age 31 or older was John Henry Johnson — and he did it twice (1962: 1,141 yds at 33; 1964: 1,048 yds at 35).
The only player of the 1960s to gain 1,000 receiving yards at age 22 or younger: Mike Ditka, 1961 — 1,076 yds at 22.
The only player of the 1960s to average 110 rushing yards a game (8+ games) was Jim Brown — and he did it twice (1963: 133.1 per game; 1965: 110.3 per game).
The only player of the 1960s to make 60 extra points: George Blanda, 1961 — 64-65 XP.
The only player of the 1960s to catch 55 passes as a running back: Charlie Harraway, 1969 — 55 rec, 489 yds.
Only two players of the 1960s threw for 3,500 yards: Joe Namath (1967: 4,007 yds); Sonny Jurgensen (2×, best 1967: 3,747 yds).
Only two players of the 1960s gained 2,300 all-purpose yards: Gale Sayers (1966: 2,440 all-purpose yds); Timmy Brown (2×, best 1963: 2,428 all-purpose yds).
The only player of the 1960s to intercept 7 passes at age 33 or older: Eddie Macon, 1960 — 9 INT at 33.
Only two players of the 1960s caught 45 passes at age 34 or older: Pete Retzlaff (1965: 66 rec at 34); Don Maynard (1969: 47 rec at 34).
Only two players of the 1960s completed 62% of their passes (250+ attempts): Bart Starr (2×, best 1962: 62.5% on 285 att); Sonny Jurgensen (1969: 62% on 442 att).
Just three players of the 1960s threw for 2,800 yards with 15 or fewer touchdowns: Joe Namath (1968: 3,147 yds, 15 TD); Norm Snead (1963: 3,043 yds, 13 TD); Jack Kemp (1963: 2,910 yds, 13 TD).
Just three players of the 1960s gained 1,000 receiving yards as a tight end: Jackie Smith (1967: 1,205 yds, 56 rec); Pete Retzlaff (1965: 1,190 yds, 66 rec); Mike Ditka (1961: 1,076 yds, 56 rec).
Just three players of the 1960s scored 140 points: Paul Hornung (2×, best 1960: 176 pts); Gino Cappelletti (2×, best 1964: 155 pts); Jim Turner (1968: 145 pts).

Just three players of the 1960s threw for 2,500 yards at age 36 or older: George Blanda (3×, best 1964: 3,287 yds at 37); Y.A. Tittle (2×, best 1962: 3,224 yds at 36); Babe Parilli (1966: 2,721 yds at 36).

Just three players of the 1960s rushed for 1,000 yards in 12 or fewer games: Jim Brown (1960: 1,257 yds in 12 games); Jim Taylor (1960: 1,101 yds in 12 games); John David Crow (1960: 1,071 yds in 12 games).

Just four players of the 1960s posted a passer rating of 100 (250+ attempts): Milt Plum (1960: 110.4 rating); Bart Starr (1966: 105 rating); Y.A. Tittle (1963: 104.8 rating); Len Dawson (1966: 101.7 rating).
Just four players of the 1960s caught 80 passes: Charley Hennigan (2×, best 1964: 101 rec); Lionel Taylor (3×, best 1961: 100 rec); Johnny Morris (1964: 93 rec); Dave Parks (1965: 80 rec).
Only two players of the 1960s ran for 8 touchdowns as a quarterback: Billy Kilmer (1961: 10 rush TD); Jack Kemp (2×, best 1960: 8 rush TD).
Only two players of the 1960s led 5 fourth-quarter comebacks: Ed Brown (1963: 6 comebacks); Norm Van Brocklin (1960: 5 comebacks).
Only two players of the 1960s recorded 2 safeties: Roger Brown (1962: 2 safeties); Ron McDole (1964: 2 safeties).

Just four players of the 1960s averaged 46 yards a punt (40+ punts): Yale Lary (2×, best 1961: 48.4 avg on 52); Bobby Joe Green (2×, best 1961: 47 avg on 73); Gary Collins (1965: 46.7 avg on 65); Bobby Walden (1964: 46.4 avg on 72).
Just four players of the 1960s made 28 field goals: Jim Turner (2×, best 1968: 34-46 FG); Jan Stenerud (1968: 30-40 FG); Pete Gogolak (1965: 28-46 FG); Bruce Gossett (1966: 28-49 FG).
Just three players of the 1960s threw 20 touchdown passes at age 23 or younger: Norm Snead (1962: 22 TD at 23); Fran Tarkenton (1962: 22 TD at 22); Bob Griese (1968: 21 TD at 23).

method: NFL before 2000: each line is one Stathead (Pro Football Reference) Season Finder query over the decade, run in a signed-in subscriber session; the result rows, with Pro Football Reference's stable player ids, are stored as provenance. Nothing recalled or estimated.

Passing, rushing and receiving are official from 1932, interceptions from 1940, sacks from 1982 (Pro Football Reference's unofficial earlier sack counts are excluded); rules on a category a decade did not record simply return nothing. The 1960s include AFL seasons, which NFL records count; the 1940s exclude the AAFC, which they do not.
